newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM's brother takes power in Punjab.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM's brother takes power in Punjab.

text.p: A brother of new Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif took power in the populous central province of Punjab on Thursday as their party appeared set to lead coalition governments in two more provinces.

Shahbaz Sharif, a year younger than the 47-year-old Nawaz Sharif, was sworn in as Punjab chief minister in the provincial capital Lahore hours after the 24-seat provincial assembly, dominated by their Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party, elected him to the office with a massive 226-7 majority.
This was the first time in Pakistan that a brother of a prime minister was also the chief executive in a province.
Nawaz, scion of a business family living in Lahore, took over as prime minister on Monday, but had yet to announce a cabinet.

The PML, which won a landslide in the general elections on February 3, also appeared certain on Thursday to lead coalition governments with its allies in the volatile southern province of Sindh and the North West Frontier province.
The party's chances of forming a coalition government in Sindh brightened after it agreed on a power-sharing formula with the Karachi-based ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).

Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP), which suffered a crushing defeat in the February 3 polls, was also in the running to lead a coalition in Sindh as the largest single party with 35 seats in the 109-seat house.
But its efforts suffered a blow from Wednesday's agreement, which gave the province's chief ministership to the 14-seat PML and the figurehead governorship to the 28-seat MQM.
The PML and its left-wing Awami National Party already had a majority in the 83-seat North West Frontier assembly, which will elect its chief minister at the weekend.
The only province with a non-PML government would be Baluchistan in the southwest, where nationalist groups had announced a majority coalition in the 43-member assembly.

Shahbaz, known in his party as a strict manager of affairs, did not formally hold any ministerial office during Nawaz's first stint as prime minister for two and half years until July 1993. But he had carried immense influence both in the centre and the then PML government in Punjab.
